spec.expr: sum by (targetId) (count_over_time({container_name="wake-on-lan"} | json | msg="Wake flag armed" [$__interval]))

spec.description: One series per target. "Wake requested" carries targetName (human-readable); "Wake flag armed" only carries targetId since it's logged one call later from the wol service. Both are emitted for every wake click, so the two series should track each other closely.
spec.title: Wakes Triggered Over Time

spec.description: Successful sends are split by WOL_SEND_METHOD (dgram is the default UDP path; wakeonlan is the CLI fallback used when dgram broadcast fails with EACCES/ENOTSUP). Failures don't carry a method field since the send never completed.
spec.title: Magic Packet Send Outcome

spec.expr: {container_name="wake-on-lan"} | json | msg="Magic packet send failed" | line_format "targetId={{.targetId}}  mac={{.mac}}  err={{.err}}"

spec.description: Full failure detail (both dgram and wakeonlan-CLI attempts have already been exhausted by the time this is logged)
spec.title: Magic Packet Failures

spec.expr: sum by (targetId, result) (count_over_time({container_name="wake-on-lan"} | json | msg="Wake flag consume checked" [$__interval]))

spec.description: One series per target/result combination. "not_woken" means the client polled outside the withinSeconds window (or before any wake was armed); "woken" confirms the target's boot was observed within the window.
spec.title: Consume Outcomes Over Time

spec.description: Total wake requests in the selected time range
spec.title: Wakes Triggered

spec.description: Requires the wake/consume rate limiters' handler to log a msg="Rate limit exceeded" line (with route, ip) when a client is throttled — express-rate-limit's default behavior is to just return HTTP 429 without a matching pino log line. Shows No data until that logging is added.
spec.title: Rate Limit Hits

spec.expr: sum by (targetId) (count_over_time({container_name="wake-on-lan"} | json | msg="Shutdown flag armed" [$__interval]))

spec.description: Mirrors Wakes Triggered Over Time. "Shutdown requested" fires only if the target's AgentConfig.shutdownEnabled is true — the route returns 400 (no log line here) otherwise, so a target with shutdown disabled will never appear.
spec.title: Shutdown Triggered / Armed

spec.expr: sum by (targetId, result) (count_over_time({container_name="wake-on-lan"} | json | msg="Shutdown flag consume checked" [$__interval]))

spec.description: Mirrors Consume Outcomes Over Time. "not_shutdown" means the agent's poll found no fresh unconsumed flag; "shutdown" confirms the agent picked one up and (on real Windows) proceeded to shut the machine down.
spec.title: Shutdown Consume Outcomes

spec.description: Total shutdown requests in the selected time range
spec.title: Shutdowns Triggered

spec.expr: sum by (targetId) (count_over_time({container_name="wake-on-lan"} | json | msg="Agent heartbeat received" [$__interval]))

spec.description: Two perspectives on the same heartbeat: the server's own "Agent heartbeat received" (container_name="wake-on-lan", the app's Docker logs) vs. the agent's own "Heartbeat sent", pushed directly to Loki from the Windows machine itself (service="agent" — no container_name, since it never goes through Docker). The two series should track each other; a gap between them is diagnostic of a network problem between the target and the NAS, not just a target that stopped running. A target that stops heartbeating entirely shows as both series dropping to zero.
spec.title: Agent Heartbeat Rate

spec.description: Errors pushed directly from the Windows agent itself — most commonly "Script execution failed" (missing/failing defaultScript, wolScript, or manualBootScript) or a network error reaching the server. Only possible because the agent ships its own logs directly to Loki; previously these would have been invisible outside a local file on the machine nobody looks at.
spec.title: Agent Errors

spec.description: Error counts by service layer (api, wol, db)
spec.title: Error Rate by Service

spec.description: Errors from the db service layer — most commonly "Database initialization failed" at startup (bad credentials, unreachable Postgres, or a missing DB_SSL_CA_PATH)
spec.title: Database Errors

spec.description: All error-level logs across all services
spec.title: Error Logs
